display.purpose: The single uncovered-exposure figure on the Cover Sheet. Mono, tabular, never used for words.

headline.purpose: The landing claim sentence only, capped at 15ch.

body.purpose: Running prose. 68ch on landing, 46ch in the Cover Sheet hero note.

quantity.purpose: Every figure in ledger, position card, decisions list and tape. Tabular mono, always.

label.purpose: Keys, units, section headings, tags. Uppercase Archivo, 0.08-0.16em tracking.

mark.purpose: The Vig wordmark. The only place tracking exceeds 0.16em.

shadows.name: knob-lift
shadows.purpose: The scrub knob only. It must read as a physical grabbable object above the rail.

shadows.name: capital-in-flight
shadows.purpose: The brass capital chip while it travels from equity into the reserve meter. Exists for ~1s per opened structure.

shadows.name: live-halo
shadows.purpose: Ring around the live-market dot. A halo, not elevation.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Default arrival easing: meter fill (0.5s), card enter (0.62s), path draw (0.9s), decision pulse (0.9s).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Number tweens (850ms). Fast commit, long settle - a sum of money arriving and coming to rest.

motion.name: ease-arc
motion.purpose: Capital chip travelling on a lifted arc from equity to the reserve meter (1100ms). An arc reads as an object with weight; a straight line reads as a UI transition.

motion.name: ease-ui
motion.purpose: Button and knob hover/active state changes.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Breach recolour across position card border, curve stroke, corridor fill, spot line and dot.

motion.name: spring-snap
motion.purpose: Slight overshoot for elements that snap into place rather than settle.

motion.name: stagger
motion.purpose: Card batch entry, so a group of arrivals reads as a sequence.

components.name: Primary CTA
components.description: The single brass action on the landing page. Brass fill, ground text, zero radius.
components.css: .ds-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 11px 20px; text-decoration: none; background: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); color: var(--ground, #0a0a0c); font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 12.5px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; border: 1px solid var(--reserved, #d8b26a); border-radius: 0; transition: background .18s ease, color .18s ease, transform .18s ease; } .ds-cta:hover { background: #e6c489; transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-cta:active { transform: none; } .ds-cta:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--reserved, #d8b26a); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost CTA
components.description: Secondary action. Never gains a background; hover raises ink and border only.
components.css: .ds-cta-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 11px 20px; text-decoration: none; background: none; color: var(--ink-dim, #918d85); font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 12.5px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; border: 1px solid var(--hair-lit, #31313d); border-radius: 0; transition: color .18s ease, border-color .18s ease; } .ds-cta-ghost:hover { color: var(--ink, #ece9e3); border-color: var(--ink-mute, #5f5c56); } .ds-cta-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--reserved, #d8b26a); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: State Tag
components.description: Outlined uppercase state marker. Outline and label always take the same state colour; never filled.
components.css: .ds-tag { display: inline-block; font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 2px 7px; border: 1px solid var(--hair-lit, #31313d); color: var(--ink-dim, #918d85); border-radius: 0; } .ds-tag-covered { color: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); border-color: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); } .ds-tag-settled { color: var(--credit, #86b06b); border-color: var(--credit, #86b06b); }

components.name: Reserve Meter
components.description: Capital reserved against its ceiling. Fill is scaled from the left edge, never resized. At zero it recolours to lit hairline so empty reads as empty.

components.css: .ds-meter { height: 6px; background: var(--raised, #16161b); border: 1px solid var(--hair, #21212a); position: relative; border-radius: 0; } .ds-meter i { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; display: block; width: 100%; transform-origin: left center; background: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); transition: transform .5s cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1); } .ds-meter i[data-empty="true"] { background: var(--hair-lit, #31313d); } .ds-meter-legend { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; color: var(--ink-mute, #5f5c56); font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size: 10.5px; margin-top: 7px; font-variant-numeric: normal; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-meter i { transition: none; } }

components.css: .ds-pos { border: 1px solid var(--hair, #21212a); background: var(--panel, #101014); padding: 16px 18px; border-radius: 0; transition: border-color .45s ease; } .ds-pos.breach { border-color: var(--breached, #c8574a); } .ds-pos-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 14px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-sym { font-family: var(--mono, monospace); font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: var(--ink, #ece9e3); } .ds-exp { color: var(--ink-mute, #5f5c56); font-size: 11px; font-family: var(--mono, monospace); } .ds-pos-nums { margin-left: auto; display: flex; gap: 22px; align-items: baseline; } .ds-pos-nums .ds-k { color: var(--ink-mute, #5f5c56); font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; display: block; } .ds-pos-nums .ds-v { font-family: var(--mono, monospace); font-size: 14px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-credit { color: var(--credit, #86b06b); } .ds-res { color: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); } .ds-floors { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-top: 8px; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--ink-mute, #5f5c56); } .ds-floors b { font-family: var(--mono, monospace); font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-win b { color: var(--credit, #86b06b); } .ds-cap b { color: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); }

components.name: Scrub Control
components.description: The landing signature control. 19px visual knob over a 44px invisible touch target; the rail shares its top edge with the curve above because they share a price axis. Pointer and keyboard.
components.css: .ds-scrub-rail { position: relative; height: 34px; cursor: ew-resize; border-top: 1px solid var(--hair, #21212a); touch-action: none; } .ds-scrub-corridor { position: absolute; top: -1px; height: 3px; background: var(--credit, #86b06b); opacity: .55; } .ds-scrub-knob { position: absolute; top: -9px; width: 19px; height: 19px; margin-left: -9.5px; padding: 0; cursor: grab; touch-action: none; background: var(--ink, #ece9e3); border: 0; border-radius: 50%; box-shadow: 0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.55); transition: transform .16s ease, background .16s ease; } .ds-scrub-knob::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 44px; height: 44px; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); } .ds-scrub-knob:hover { transform: scale(1.14); } .ds-scrub-knob:active { cursor: grabbing; transform: scale(1.06); } .ds-scrub-knob:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid var(--reserved, #d8b26a); outline-offset: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-scrub-knob { transition: none; } }

components.css: .ds-decisions { border: 1px solid var(--hair, #21212a); background: var(--panel, #101014); } .ds-dec { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 108px 92px 1fr; gap: 14px; padding: 9px 16px; align-items: baseline; font-size: 12px; font-family: var(--sans, Archivo, sans-serif); } .ds-dec + .ds-dec { border-top: 1px solid var(--hair, #21212a); } .ds-bucket { font-family: var(--mono, monospace); color: var(--ink-dim, #918d85); font-size: 11.5px; } .ds-verb { font-size: 10px; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-why { color: var(--ink-dim, #918d85); } .ds-submitted .ds-verb { color: var(--credit, #86b06b); } .ds-refused .ds-verb { color: var(--reserved, #d8b26a); } .ds-would .ds-verb { color: var(--working, #6b8caf); } @media (max-width: 860px) { .ds-dec { grid-template-columns: 1fr auto; row-gap: 3px; } .ds-why { grid-column: 1 / -1; } }

narrative.overview:
Vig looks like the document a risk desk prints at the close of the session, not like a trading app. The surfaces are dark because of the scene rather than the category — this is read on a desk beside a broker dashboard, in a room where the screen is the brightest object — and the ink is bone (#ece9e3) rather than white, so the page reads as paper under lamplight instead of as an LCD. Nothing is rounded, nothing is shadowed, nothing is decorated. Structure is carried entirely by one hairline (#21212a) and by two background steps above the ground.

The system's whole discipline is that colour is not a palette. Every accent is a statement about capital: brass is money set aside, green is money collected, red is a strike that broke, blue-grey is an order still working. There is no brand colour, no gradient, and no hue that means "primary". Any surface that adopts these tokens without the mechanic behind them is misusing them.

Density is high and deliberate. Body type sits at 13px, labels at 10-11px, and the only type allowed to be large is a quantity: the uncovered-exposure figure on the Cover Sheet (up to 84px) and the landing claim. Every number is IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures, because every number on these surfaces is compared against another number and proportional digits make columns drift.
keyCharacteristics: Zero-radius rectangles, hairline rules, no shadow vocabulary except one in-flight chip
Two accent families with fixed meanings (brass = reserved, green = collected) and one forbidden-elsewhere red
Mono for all quantities, Archivo for all labels; never the reverse
Motion only as consequence — nothing loops, nothing idles
Dark ground with bone ink; browser chrome (selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring) themed to match

rules.name: The Mechanic Rule
rules.body: Colour is derived from the product mechanic, never chosen as a palette. Before introducing any colour, name the account state it reports. If there is no state, use ink.

rules.name: The Red Is Breach Rule
rules.body: Red means a breached strike or a realised loss, and it is permitted nowhere else. It is never an error colour for form validation, never a destructive-button colour, never a chart series. A red pixel on a Vig surface is a claim about money.

rules.name: The Brass-On-Ground Rule
rules.body: Brass is a background only when the foreground is ground (#0a0a0c) — CTA, capital chip, selection. Brass text sits on panel or ground, never on brass.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every quantity carries .n — IBM Plex Mono with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. tabular-nums is also set on body as a floor. Figures in adjacent rows must share an advance width; a proportional digit in a blotter is a bug.

rules.name: The Two-Job Rule
rules.body: Mono is for quantities, Archivo is for language. A label never uses mono (the meter legend explicitly resets .n back to Archivo when its digits are prose, not a column), and a quantity never uses Archivo.

rules.name: The Size-Is-Importance Rule
rules.body: Type scale is a claim about what matters. Only one figure per surface earns display size, and on the Cover Sheet that figure is uncovered exposure — the number the product exists to show. It never moves and never shrinks at mobile.

rules.name: The One Spine Rule
rules.body: Every landing block shares the 1180px/24px measure. Narrow reading columns are achieved by capping children (max-width: 68ch), never by centring a smaller container — a shifted left edge reads as a different page.

rules.name: The Figure Survives Rule
rules.body: Responsive behaviour removes labels and secondary items before it shrinks a number. The uncovered-exposure figure and the reserve state keep their size at every width.

rules.name: The Flat Report Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat. If a new element needs separation, use a hairline or the next tonal step — never a shadow. A shadow is permitted only on something that is literally in motion or something grabbable.

rules.name: The No-Radius Rule
rules.body: Radius is 0 unless the element is circular by function (a dot, a knob) or is in flight (the 2px chip). There is no "rounded card" in this system.

rules.name: The Outline-State Rule
rules.body: A state is shown by recolouring a 1px outline and its label together, never by filling a pill with a background.

rules.name: The Caused-Motion Rule
rules.body: Every animation is caused by something that actually happened in the account. Nothing loops, nothing idles, nothing animates to fill silence. Numbers tween with expo-out over 850ms; capital travels on a lifted arc from equity into the reserve meter over 1100ms and the meter brightens on impact; payoff paths draw stroke-first over 900ms; cards enter staggered at 70ms per index. Every one of these is behind prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.name: The Empty Is Designed Rule
rules.body: No component ships without a zero state that says why it is empty. An empty meter changes colour; an empty list states the market's status.

dos: Do name the account state before choosing a colour. Brass = reserved, green = collected, red = breached, blue-grey = working.
Do set every quantity in IBM Plex Mono with tabular-nums via .n.
Do keep radius at 0 for everything that is not a dot, a knob, or the in-flight capital chip (2px).
Do separate surfaces with a 1px hairline (#21212a) or the next tonal step, in that order.
Do show state by recolouring a 1px outline and its label together.
Do animate a value only when the account changed it, and always with a prefers-reduced-motion escape.
Do give small controls an invisible 44px touch target rather than growing the visual control.
Do hold the 1180px / 24px spine; narrow a column by capping children at a ch measure, not by re-centring.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces — selection, caret, scrollbar, focus ring — with system tokens.
Do design the empty state with its reason; the market is closed most of the time.
donts: Don't use red for anything but a breached strike or a realised loss. It is not an error colour, not a destructive-action colour, not a chart series.
Don't introduce a colour that has no mechanic behind it, including a "brand" hue or any gradient.
Don't add a shadow to a surface. Shadows belong only to something in motion or something grabbable.
Don't loop, idle, or pulse an animation on a timer. If the account did nothing, the page is still.
Don't set a label in mono or a quantity in Archivo.
Don't shrink a figure to fit a small screen; drop labels and secondary items first.
Don't fill a tag or chip with a background colour; outline it.
Don't use pure white — ink is bone (#ece9e3).
Don't turn refusals into a lesser visual class than fills; they share the list, the grid and the weight.
